questions.problem:
What is the explicit formula for the $n$th term of the geometric sequence given by

$$
f(n+1)=-5f(n),\,\,f(1)=8,\,\,n\ge 1?
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The explicit formula for the $n$th term of a geometric sequence is

$$
f(n)=f(1)\cdot {r}^{n-1},\,n\ge 1.
$$

So, we must determine the first term $f(1)$ and the common ratio $r.$

We are given that the first term is $f(1)=8.$ To find the common ratio, we compare the given sequence with the general recursive formula for a geometric sequence:

$$
f(n+1)=r\cdot f(n)
$$

 

From the above, we see that $r=-5.$

Substituting $f(1)=8$ and $r=-5$ into the formula for the $n$th term, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(n) & =f(1)\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\  & =8\cdot (-5)^{n-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the formula for the $n$th term is

$$
f(n)=8\cdot (-5)^{n-1},\,n\ge 1.
$$

questions.problem:
The formula for the $n$th term of a geometric sequence is $f(n)=\frac{3}{4}\cdot {8}^{n}$ for $n\ge 1.$ What is the recursive formula for this sequence? Express your answer in terms of $f(n).$

$f(n+1)=$
{{field-1}}$,\,f(1)=$
{{field-2}}$,\,n\ge 1$
questions.worked_solution:
The recursive formula for a geometric sequence is

$$
f(n+1)=r\cdot f(n).
$$

To complete the formula, we must determine the common ratio $r$ and state the first term $f(1).$ The first two terms are

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) & =\frac{3}{4}\cdot {8}^{1}=\frac{3}{4}\cdot 8=6, \\ f(2) & =\frac{3}{4}\cdot {8}^{2}=\frac{3}{4}\cdot 64=48.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the common ratio is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=\frac{f(2)}{f(1)}=\frac{48}{6}=8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the recursive formula for the geometric sequence is

$$
f(n+1)=8f(n),\,f(1)=6,\,n\ge 1.
$$

questions.problem:
The formula for the $n$th term of a geometric sequence is $f(n)=\frac{10}{(-5)^{n-1}}$ for $n\ge 1.$ What is the recursive formula for this sequence? Express your answer in terms of $f(n).$

$f(n+1)=$
{{field-1}}$,\,f(1)=$
{{field-2}}$,\,n\ge 1$
questions.worked_solution:
The recursive formula for a geometric sequence is

$$
f(n+1)=r\cdot f(n).
$$

To complete the formula, we must determine the common ratio $r$ and state the first term $f(1).$ The first two terms are

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) & =\frac{10}{(-5)^{1-1}}=\frac{10}{1}=10, \\ f(2) & =\frac{10}{(-5)^{2-1}}=\frac{10}{(-5)}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the common ratio is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\frac{f(2)}{f(1)}=\frac{-2}{10}=-\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the recursive formula for the geometric sequence is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(n+1) & =-\frac{1}{5}f(n),\,f(1)=10,\,n\ge 1.\end{aligned}
$$
